title: Natural all-period fibres for a realized filtration diagram
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ with finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$ and algebraic closure $k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Omega:\operatorname{Type}(u+1)$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$; write $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $R$ be any normalized classical realization [def-zl-normalized-classical-weil-realization]. Use the classical Weil category, exact classical and finite-stage filtrations, finite point fibres and normalized local operators of [def-zl-classical-weil-filtration-transport-data, def-zl-classical-local-fibre-comparison]. Let $F$ be a classical filtration of length $r$, $E\subset\Omega$ a finite coefficient field and $M$ an exact finite-stage Weil filtration. Suppose Weil isomorphisms $a_j:M_j\otimes_E\Omega\simeq R(F_j)$ and $b_j:Q_j\otimes_E\Omega\simeq R(S_j)$ are given and intertwine every prescribed inclusion and quotient arrow. There exist ZlClassicalFibreComparison data for every term and quotient of these SAME models, intertwining the normalized local operators for every positive return period. Their fibre isomorphisms are simultaneously natural for every inclusion and quotient arrow: applying the extended finite fibre map and then the target comparison equals applying the source comparison and then the actual classical fibre map. No existence of $E,M,a,b$, new exactness or weight assertion is claimed.

source.place: Paragraph 1: the actual Weil filtration and its local purity; Bhatt--Scholze Section 6.8, especially 6.8.4(1),(4), 6.8.14(2), 6.8.15.

proof.text:
To use the currently small-coefficient two-fibre API, choose an algebraic closure of Q_l in the scheme universe, use its algebraic-closure equivalence with Omega and transport finite subfields and tensor fibre comparisons along it; the finite-level germ/unit formulas are preserved. 1. For each finite-stage term and quotient, compose its normalized extended H^0
point-fibre identification with the fibre of its supplied Weil isomorphism a or b.
Then use the normalized comparison for the supplied R, on the corresponding
classical object. This is the same comparison at all positive return periods.
The normalized_two_fibre_comparison fixes coefficient extension and point sections
on finite-level germs and inverse-limit projections, so no new fibre path is chosen.

2. Apply classical_local_frobenius_iterate_comparison to R. Its factor squares
intertwine point transport, the semilinear return compositor and iterated Weil maps.
Identify the orbit-point recursion with the positive-power endpoints inductively.
The finite-etale reparametrization at the return, followed by that endpoint equality,
sends each cover lift z to the specified point Frobenius composite. This gives the
existential beta and the local_operator field for every term and quotient.

3. Naturality of normalized point pullback, H^0, ulift and scalar extension takes
ha and hb to their corresponding fibre squares. Cancel the intermediate normalized
isomorphisms. Naturality of the comparison for R yields exactly the two displayed
identities, including zero maps and arbitrary quotient ranks. If r=0 there are no
quotient or arrow squares; if Y is empty all the point assertions are vacuous.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.8, assembly of the existing normalized realization interfaces for blueprint real-mixed-by-curves paragraph 1

theorem zl_classical_filtration_diagram_fibres
    (R : ZlClassicalRealization D l hl Ω Y₀)
    (r : ℕ) (F : ZlClassicalFiltration D l Ω Y₀ r)
    (E : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω)
    (M : ZlFiniteFiltration D l hl Ω Y₀ r E)
    (a : ∀ j : Fin (r + 1), sfWeilStageObject D l hl Y₀ Ω E (M.terms j) ≅
      ((R.weil D l hl Ω Y₀).obj (F.terms j)).obj)
    (b : ∀ j : Fin r, sfWeilStageObject D l hl Y₀ Ω E (M.quotients j) ≅
      ((R.weil D l hl Ω Y₀).obj (F.quotients j)).obj)
    (ha : ∀ j : Fin r,
      (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion E).map
          (M.inclusion j).hom.f ≫ (a j.succ).hom.hom.f =
        (a j.castSucc).hom.hom.f ≫
          ((R.weil D l hl Ω Y₀).map (F.inclusion j)).hom.hom.f)
    (hb : ∀ j : Fin r,
      (GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.inclusion E).map
          (M.quotient j).hom.f ≫ (b j).hom.hom.f =
        (a j.succ).hom.hom.f ≫
          ((R.weil D l hl Ω Y₀).map (F.quotient j)).hom.hom.f) :
    ∃ (c : ∀ j : Fin (r + 1),
        ZlClassicalFibreComparison D l hl Ω Y₀ E (M.terms j) (F.terms j))
      (d : ∀ j : Fin r,
        ZlClassicalFibreComparison D l hl Ω Y₀ E (M.quotients j) (F.quotients j)),
      (∀ (j : Fin r) (x : Spec (.of D.k) ⟶ (D.geometricFiber Y₀).left),
        zlFiniteFibreMap D l hl Ω Y₀ E (M.inclusion j) x ≫
            ((c j.succ).fibre x).hom =
          ((c j.castSucc).fibre x).hom ≫
            etaleAlgebraicFiberMap l Ω x (F.inclusion j).hom.f) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin r) (x : Spec (.of D.k) ⟶ (D.geometricFiber Y₀).left),
        zlFiniteFibreMap D l hl Ω Y₀ E (M.quotient j) x ≫
            ((d j).fibre x).hom =
          ((c j.succ).fibre x).hom ≫
            etaleAlgebraicFiberMap l Ω x (F.quotient j).hom.f)
